::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
One of China's three major OSAT firms alongside JCET and Tongfu, founded December 2003 with roots in a state-owned enterprise; its largest shareholder, Tianshui Huatian Microelectronics Co., holds 23%, with the remaining float heavily retail-owned (57%) — an unusually dispersed ownership structure for a Chinese semiconductor firm of this scale. Earnings accelerated sharply in 2026: Q1 revenue reached ¥4.8 billion (+34.5% YoY), and the company guided H1 2026 net profit to ¥750-850 million, up 231-275% year-on-year, crediting advanced-packaging mix shift and M&A integration.
:::

**Chinese name:** 华天科技 (Huátiān Kējì)

## What does this facility make?

Chip assembly, test, and wafer-level/advanced packaging services, now spanning SiP, flip-chip, TSV, bumping, fan-out (FO), wafer/panel-level packaging (WLP/PLP), and 2.5D/3D integration.

## Why does it matter?

Based in Gansu province — a notable geographic outlier among China's semiconductor firms, most of which cluster in the Yangtze River Delta (Jiangsu/Shanghai) or Pearl River Delta (Guangdong) regions. Its 2026 earnings jump, alongside JCET's and Tongfu's, points to a sector-wide advanced-packaging upcycle among China's three major OSATs rather than a single-company story.
